rationale:
Evidence: iteration 10 is the best raced design (231.83). Its oval finish rate rose to 5 of 20 from 1 of 20, and max error fell to about 0.0585 m on the oval, just inside the 0.06 m limit. Its s-bend and slalom still end off track, with s-bend progress at 0.49 and 1.3 line-loss events on the slalom. The change that moved the result was the physical yaw response (wheel_track 0.12 to 0.09 and mass 0.8 to 0.55), so steering authority per PWM count is the lever that is working. Earlier sensor, gain and footprint changes had no measurable effect, and the off-track limit cannot rise because body_width/4 + 0.0125 stays below 0.06 m for every allowed width.

Changes: (1) wheel_track reduced from 0.09 to 0.08 m, the contract minimum. Turn rate per unit wheel-speed difference rises by about 12.5 percent, which gives more correction at the bends where the line is lost. (2) mass reduced from 0.55 to 0.45 kg, which lowers yaw inertia and speeds the response to the same turn command. (3) kp raised from 5.0 to 5.5 to match the stronger steering per PWM. (4) kd kept at 0.8 to damp the faster yaw, and ki 0.5 and base_speed 1.0 are kept as the proven settings. Sensors and weights are unchanged, so only the physical response and the proportional gain move.

Expected result: lower max error and fewer line-loss events on the s-bend, which should lift the oval finish rate above 5 of 20 and raise s-bend progress. Some risk of oscillation from the faster yaw, which kd 0.8 should contain. Completion on the s-bend or slalom remains unlikely this round.
